A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WEDGE/PERFFORGE research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original CodeContests experiments, component ablations, constraint analyses, and evaluations involving EFFI-LEARNER and PIE, with additional results and case studies in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds evaluated PerfFuzz comparisons and a phase-level resource-cost analysis.

M1.justification: The contrastive profiling, constraint synthesis and instrumentation, constraint-aware mutator generation, and AFL++ search remain unchanged. The retry-limit revision and prompt-number corrections concern settings and documentation rather than a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same CodeContests coverage, including 154 problems and 33,020 C++ programs, the 56-problem/280-Python-solution utility evaluation, and retained case studies. GSO and real-world projects enter the discussion, not the evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: PerfFuzz, previously cited but not evaluated, becomes an additional comparator in Tables 1, 4, and 5 and Figure 3. Existing EVALPERF variants, TG-prompt, utility methods, and component ablations remain. The input-size comparison in Table 6 retains its original comparator set.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 changes the stated maximum mutator-repair budget from five to ten rounds. Because v1 already reported success after ten rounds, this establishes a reported-setting correction, not that experiments were rerun. Dataset filtering, performance metrics, and the one-hour fuzzing budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.4 and Table 7 analyze which WEDGE phases consume time and tokens and report amortized costs. Existing component ablations, constraint-discrimination analysis, input-size sensitivity results, and Appendix C case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging instruction counts over five runs, Mann–Whitney tests at the same significance threshold, and the same variability discussion. Mutator-repair rounds are an execution budget, not statistical repetitions; no new uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced.

E6.justification: v3 adds PerfFuzz results, including 3.29×10^8 average instructions and 140.63 ms average runtime, plus resource-cost results. WEDGE's main-table win rate changes from 59% to 60% under the expanded comparator set, while its instruction and runtime averages remain unchanged. Section 4.2 corrects which variant produces slower tests in the 63.02% ablation finding. Utility and input-size results are retained.

T1.justification: The formal stress-test objective, constraint definitions, framework equations, and complexity reasoning in the case studies are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: constraint-guided performance-test generation, the PERFFORGE benchmark, and improved evaluation and guidance of code optimization. The PerfFuzz evidence and clearer attribution of the 84.5% figure support existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 clarifies that the initial slow input need not already be performance-stressing and explains why PerfFuzz's existing coverage signals may miss implementation-specific bottlenecks. It adds an amortized-cost interpretation and removes Appendix B.3's tentative explanation involving TG-prompt's generic edge-case bias. The three principal limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B.4 newly documents phase-level time and token costs, including 9,633.16 tokens for constraint reasoning/checker generation and 6,905.27 for mutator generation. Appendix A.2 revises the retry limit, and Appendix E.3 corrects decimal representations of powers of ten. Hardware, model versions, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands research positioning through additions to Section 2.1 and a new Section 5 covering performance fuzzing, performance-bug detection, and LLM-assisted testing. It discusses repository-level GSO and distinguishes WEDGE's synthesized local predicates from other testing approaches. All 52 earlier references are retained, with 28 additional entries.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose and terminology edits, expands overview and baseline explanations, adds a dedicated related-work section and acknowledgements, and inserts Appendix B.4. The main methodological narrative and existing appendix organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 7, expands Tables 1, 4, and 5 with PerfFuzz rows, and replaces Figure 3(c)'s EVALPERFRAND comparison with PerfFuzz. EVALPERFRAND's numerical comparison remains in Table 5. Captions, table formatting, hyperlinks, and float placement receive limited adjustments.

improvement.justification: The added specialized-fuzzer comparison, fuller research positioning, cost breakdown, and corrections to the ablation statement and retry limit provide useful, targeted improvements. Reporting weaknesses limit the gain: Table 1 now says 60% while Section 4.2 retains 59%, and Table 7 labels 99.65 as input-pair-mining executions whereas B.4 uses it as generated inputs when amortizing costs. These issues temper, but do not outweigh, the added evidence and clarity.
